title: Token Detail Page Layout
heading: Token Detail Page Layout
text: Click into any token and this is the page you land on. Signal stream on the left, K-line chart in the middle, order panel on the right, function tabs at the bottom — first get clear on where each region is, then see how the two hands-on dashboards are set up: the Stage-2 Signal dashboard and the Trenches dashboard.

title: Token Detail Page Layout
heading: The Page Is Split Into Four Regions
text: Left to right, top to bottom — that's all the regions on the detail page. 1 Left · Live Signal Stream A continuously scrolling signal list. Each entry shows the token name, market cap, number of signals, time elapsed, and the max gain since the first alert. Click any entry to jump to that token's detail page. The whole column can be collapsed from the top-left corner. 2 Middle · Main K-Line Chart Timeframes range from 1s to 1d ; the second-level timeframes are for chasing fast-moving tokens. VWAP is overlaid on the chart, with volume and two AO momentum indicators below it. The top-right corner toggles between Price / Market Cap and USD / SOL display modes. ⚠ These two toggles only render the chip distribution chart correctly when set to USD + Market Cap . Switching away from that combination will make the K-line, chip distribution peaks, and indicators all behave incorrectly. 3 Right · Trading Panel + Holder Structure The top half covers buy/sell, market/limit orders, quick amounts, and take-profit/stop-loss. The "Featured Metrics" section in the bottom half shows this token's wallet holder structure — how much is held by high-frequency traders, new wallets, old wallets, blue-chip top winners, smart money, and junk wallets. These figures are the core basis for judging whether a token's holder base is clean. 4 Bottom · Function Tabs + Global Entry Points The tab bar has Trade Details, Signal Analysis, DCA/Limit Analysis, Positions, Open Orders, Trade History, and My Strategies. The very bottom row is the global entry bar: Watchlist, Signals , Hot, Monitor, Positions, Trenches, AI Strategy — the Signal dashboard opens right from here. There are three known chart gotchas — if "the chart looks wrong," check these first: 1. Chip distribution only works with USD + Market Cap

title: Token Detail Page Layout
heading: Bottom Global Entry Points
text: No need to go back to the home page — the bottom row of the detail page switches dashboards directly. The two most-used ones are "Signals" and "Trenches." 1 "Signals" — Signal Dashboard 信号 (Signals) is the leftmost item in the bottom row. Click it to open the Signal dashboard, where the filtering, sorting, and screening for all six signal types is configured. See Custom Filtering for the Six Signals → for setup instructions. 2 "Trenches" — Trenches Dashboard 战壕 (Trenches), further along the same row — click it and the left column switches to the Trenches list, split into three stages: 新创建 (Newly Created) / 即将迁移 (About to Migrate) / 已迁移 (Migrated).

title: Token Detail Page Layout
heading: Sub-Topic: The Stage-2 Signal Dashboard
text: Find tokens that spiked past $150K within the last 24 hours, have since pulled back, but are still holding above $50K — a "stage-2" runner that already had its first move and hasn't died yet. The Idea "Stage 1" is the run from zero to the initial peak, which most people miss. "Stage 2" is betting there's a second wave after the pullback from that peak. So the conditions need to lock down three things at once: it really did spike (all-time-high market cap ≥ 150K), it's still alive (current market cap ≥ 50K), and it's still fresh enough (token age ≤ 24 hours). Then use two wallet-structure metrics to filter out manipulated and junk tokens. Standard Metrics Current mkt cap ≥ 50 · ATH ≥ 150 Token age ≤ 1440 In "Filter Settings" → Standard Metrics tab, fill in three fields. Featured Metrics Screenshot pending · stage2-feature Switch to the Featured Metrics tab and fill in two wallet-structure conditions. Full Parameters Tab Parameter Value Why This Setting Launch Platform Pump / LetsBonk 1 / LetsBonk 2 Check 3 boxes Only look at mainstream launch platforms — other platforms are too noisy Standard Metrics Current Market Cap ($K) Min 50 Still holding up after the pullback, hasn't gone to zero Standard Metrics All-Time-High Market Cap ($K) Min 150 Genuinely spiked once and had market consensus Standard Metrics Token Age (min) Max 1440 1440 min = 24 hours — only look at tokens created today Featured Metrics New Wallet Holdings (%) Max 70 Too high a share held by new wallets often means a batch of alt accounts running a manipulated setup Featured Metrics Junk Wallet Holdings (%) Max 5 Loosened to 5% to leave some margin — genuine big runners are mostly under 1% Once all six fields are filled in, the "Signal Filter" indicator at the top of the popup will show 6 , the Launch Platfo

title: Token Detail Page Layout
heading: Sub-Topic: The Trenches Dashboard
text: Stage-2 waits for a token to finish a full run before getting in. Trenches camps out before the token even starts running. The filter popups for the two dashboards look completely different — don't try to reuse the Signal dashboard's setup here. Three Stages, Three Sets of Conditions Trenches splits tokens into three stages by lifecycle, and those are the three tabs at the top of the popup. Each stage has its own filter conditions — whichever stage tab you're on, what you fill in below applies only to that stage. 1 Newly Created Tokens that just launched and are still on the internal bonding-curve market. This stage is the noisiest — whether you can find anything worthwhile depends entirely on your filter conditions. 2 About to Migrate Tokens whose internal market is nearly full and about to move to the external market. This is the stage for getting positioned ahead of time. 3 Migrated Tokens that have already graduated to the external market. Liquidity has picked up, and there's more data to judge by. The configuration below is set on this stage. The number on each tab = how many conditions have been set for that stage , not how many tokens matched. In the screenshot, "Migrated" shows 5 , which breaks down as 1 condition for Launch Platform + 2 for Featured Metrics + 2 for Standard Metrics; "About to Migrate" shows 1 , meaning only one condition is currently set for that stage. The numbers for all three stages are independent of each other. Standard Metrics Current mkt cap ≥ 30 Token age ≤ 500 Switch to "Migrated," then in the Standard Metrics tab fill in two fields: current market cap min 30 , token age max 500 . Featured Metrics New wallets ≤ 70 · Junk wallets ≤ 10 In the Featured Metrics tab, fill in two wallet-structure fields: new wallet holdings max 70 , junk wal

All Getting Started Troubleshooting Signal System Dashboard Setup Risk Management UI Operations Getting Started How do I buy Credits? Credits are the usage fee for the AI strategy engine. You buy them on the Use Credits panel on the "API Key Management" page, in two steps. Step 1: Top up. In the top-right of the panel, click 充值 (Top Up), choose the Solana chain + SOL , and transfer 0.5 SOL to the wallet address that pops up. Note the warning: this address only supports Solana mainnet deposits — do not transfer cross-chain. Top-up dialog: choose the chain, choose SOL, then transfer to the address below the QR code. Step 2: Purchase. Once the funds arrive, click 购买 100K @ 0.5 SOL (Buy 100K @ 0.5 SOL) on the right side of the panel — 0.5 SOL buys 100K Credits . The green button pointed to by the red arrow is the purchase entry point; you can adjust the quantity on the left. How long does 100K last? Click Credits 账单 (Credits Billing) in the top-left of the panel to see line-by-line consumption records (strategy usage fees). Based on actual usage: running a single 1.5-segment strategy, 100K lasts about 4 days; running a single Wake-up Signal strategy lasts about 5 days. Running multiple strategies shortens this proportionally, so remember to top up before you run out. Consumption billing: each entry is a strategy usage fee, ranging from a few to over a hundred Credits. title: FAQ
heading: Troubleshooting The candlestick chart looks wrong, the holder-distribution bar is off, or indicators display incorrectly — what do I do?
text: First check the two display toggles at the top. Holder distribution only supports the USD + 市值 (Market Cap) combination — switching to SOL pricing or 价格 (Price) basis can cause the candlestick chart, holder-distribution bar, and indicators to all break. The toggles are to the right of the timeframe row: USD / SOL and 价格 / 市值 (Price / Market Cap). If something looks wrong, switch them back to USD and 市值 (Market Cap) first — that fixes it in most cases. The red box marks the USD / SOL and 价格 / 市值 (Price / Market Cap) toggles.

title: FAQ
heading: Troubleshooting The holder-distribution bar suddenly disappeared entirely?
text: It's most likely because you clicked log in the bottom-right corner. Once the chart switches to a logarithmic scale, the candlestick chart displays incorrectly and the holder-distribution bar on the right simply disappears. log sits in the bottom-right of the chart, to the right of the timestamp, next to % and 自动 (Auto). Click it again to toggle it off and everything comes back. With log enabled, the Y-axis switches to a logarithmic scale and the holder-distribution bar disappears. Click the marked log button again to restore it. This button is easy to hit by accident while zooming the chart — if the holder-distribution bar vanishes, check here first.

title: FAQ
heading: Troubleshooting An indicator disappeared, or the chart panes above/below got scrambled?
text: Check whether you accidentally touched the three dots to the right of a header. The candlestick chart and every indicator header (e.g. "Volume WMA 1") has a ⋯ menu after it, and two items in that menu can mess up your chart: 隐藏 (Hide) — immediately hides that candlestick series or indicator, so it disappears from the chart entirely. The move up/down options inside 移动到 (Move To) — moves the indicator to a different pane, scrambling the top-to-bottom order of the main chart and sub-charts. The ⋯ menu after an indicator header: choosing Hide removes the indicator from view, while Move To can scramble the pane order. "隐藏" (Hide) and "移除" (Remove) sit next to each other in the menu, so a slip of the hand can easily hit the wrong one. The "对象树… (Object Tree…)" option in the menu lists everything currently on the chart — check there if something has gone missing. If you're not sure, don't click around randomly in this menu — use the row at the top to change the display basis instead of touching the header.

title: FAQ
heading: Troubleshooting The candlestick chart is invisible, indicators are wrong, and none of the above fixes work?
text: The ultimate fix: clear the local cache . The display state of the candlestick chart and indicators is stored locally in your browser — once that cache gets corrupted, no amount of toggling will save it. Clearing it and reloading fixes it. The option lives behind the gear icon (Settings) on the right of the top bar: open it, find "清空本地缓存" (Clear Local Cache), click the red 清空 (Clear) button, then refresh the page. Top bar gear icon → Clear Local Cache → 清空 (Clear) — the two red arrows mark these spots.

title: FAQ
heading: Signal System What exactly are the six signals?
text: Early Pick, Wake-up Signal, Post-Pullback Rebound Signal, Wallets I Follow, Blue-chip Top Winner Wallet Resonance, and X (Twitter) Lead Car. You can enable all six, or keep just one. When only one is kept, the signal list becomes a dedicated dashboard for that signal type.

title: FAQ
heading: Signal System How do I view just one signal type?
text: Click the "Signal Type" dropdown at the top and uncheck the other five, leaving only the one you want. The number to the right of the dropdown updates accordingly — for example, it shows 1 when only one is kept. See the full step-by-step guide: Customizing the Six Signal Filters →

title: FAQ
heading: Signal System What's the difference between "Early Pick Count (24H)" and "Time Since Latest Pick (min)"?
text: One controls frequency , the other controls freshness — they're only meaningful when used together. 早期精选次数(24H) (Early Pick Count (24H)) — set a minimum value: how many times it was picked in the last 24 hours; a higher count means more sustained attention. 最新精选距今时长(分) (Time Since Latest Pick (min)) — set a maximum value: how long ago it was last picked; setting 60 means only within the last hour. Filtering by count alone without capping the time will surface a bunch of coins that were hot yesterday but have already cooled off.

title: FAQ
heading: Dashboard Setup How do I bring up the trending list?
text: Two steps: keep all six signal types selected , then click the sort icon in the top-right of the list and choose 24小时热度 (24H Heat) under "Sort by Token". This is what the community usually calls the trending list — it doesn't care about signal type, it just shows whichever coins are hottest overall right now.

title: FAQ
heading: Dashboard Setup What does the green number on the filter dialog's tab label mean?
text: It's how many conditions have been set under that tab , not how many coins were matched. A lot of people misread this the first time. For example, if the War Room dashboard's "Migrated" tab shows 5 , that breaks down as: 1 condition under Launch Platform + 2 under Featured Metrics + 2 under General Metrics. After filling everything in, check these numbers against each other to make sure you haven't missed anything. The War Room's three stages (New / About to Migrate / Migrated) are each counted independently and don't affect one another.

title: FAQ
heading: Dashboard Setup What's a good value for token age?
text: The unit is minutes , entered in the "Max" field. Two common presets: 1440 = 24 hours — shows only coins from today; used for the second-stage dashboard. 500 ≈ 8 hours — shows only coins that just launched; used for the War Room dashboard.

title: FAQ
heading: Dashboard Setup Can I save my filter settings to reuse next time?
text: Yes. The bottom of the filter dialog has "Template", "Import", "Export", and "Save". "Confirm" applies the filter for this session only; "Save" stores it as a template you can load directly next time. Once you've got a setup you like, it's best to save it right away — otherwise you'll have to re-enter everything when you switch dashboards and come back.

title: FAQ
heading: Dashboard Setup What if the filtered results are too few / too many?
text: The parameters aren't fixed — adjust them in this direction: Too few results — lower the minimum on "count"-type fields, and widen the maximum on "time since" fields. Too much noise — tighten them the other way. It's best to run the tutorial's default values for a day first, get a feel for it, then fine-tune at your own pace.

title: FAQ
heading: Risk Management How much junk-wallet holding is considered safe?
text: This is a hard rule. Genuine moonshots are almost always under 1% ; anything over 5% can basically be skipped outright, without even bothering to check the chart. The two values given in the tutorial already include a margin: the second-stage signal dashboard tightens it to 5 , while the War Room dashboard relaxes it to 10 — at the War Room stage, the pool hasn't been fully cleaned up yet, so the bar is set a bit looser, but that's as far as it goes.

title: FAQ
heading: Risk Management Is a high new-wallet holding automatically a bad sign?
text: Not necessarily. Newly launched coins naturally have a lot of new wallets , so this metric alone isn't conclusive. It's a soft threshold: above 70% you should be cautious, since it's often a sign of a coordinated scheme run by a batch of throwaway accounts. But it only becomes reliable when read together with junk-wallet holding — high new-wallet with low junk-wallet may just mean the coin is new; both being high is what you actually want to avoid.

title: FAQ
heading: Risk Management What do all those wallet-holding percentages on the right side mean?
text: In the "Featured Metrics" panel on the right of the token detail page, this is a breakdown of the coin's holder structure: high-frequency wallets, new wallets, old wallets, blue-chip top winner wallets, smart-money wallets, junk wallets, AMM wallets, and exchange wallets. These numbers are the core basis for judging whether the pool is clean, and they're exactly what the "Featured Metrics" tab in the filter dialog lets you filter on.

title: FAQ
heading: UI Operations Where do I open the signal dashboard and the War Room dashboard?
text: Both are in the global entry bar along the bottom row of the token detail page: Watchlist, Signals, Trending, Monitor, Positions, War Room, AI Strategy. Click "Signals" to open the signal dashboard, click "War Room" to open the War Room dashboard — no need to go back to the home page. For an explanation of each area of the page, see Token Detail Page Layout →

title: FAQ
heading: UI Operations Why do the filter dialogs for the signal dashboard and the War Room dashboard look different?
text: Because they filter different things — don't apply one dashboard's mental model to the other. Signal dashboard : the top section is "Signal Filter", centered on the count and time-since fields for the six signals. War Room dashboard : the top section is the three stages "New / About to Migrate / Migrated", each with its own conditions — there's no signal-count-style field here. What they share are the Launch Platform, Featured Metrics, and General Metrics sections.

title: FAQ
heading: UI Operations What do the War Room's "New / About to Migrate / Migrated" stages each mean?
text: Three stages split by the token's lifecycle: New — just launched, still on the internal order book. The noisiest stage. About to Migrate — the internal order book is nearly full and about to move to the external market. The position to stake out ahead of time. Migrated — already graduated to the external market, liquidity has picked up, and there's more data to base a judgment on.

title: Custom Filtering for the Six Signal Types
heading: The Six Signal Types
text: In the 信号类型 (Signal Type) dropdown you can check just one type, and the signal list will show only that type. Early Pick Wake-up Signal Post-pullback Rebound Signal Watched Wallets Blue-chip Top Wallet Resonance X (Twitter) Lead Buyer The first two already have step-by-step tutorials with screenshots — click to jump straight to the relevant steps. The other four are filtered the exact same way; tutorials for them will be added over time.

title: Custom Filtering for the Six Signal Types
heading: Screenshots: Step by Step
text: Using the "Signal Scanner" (信号扫链) board as an example: show only Early Pick signals, and require them to be fresh enough. Signal Scanner (信号扫链) · Early Pick Back from the Dead (死而复生) · Wake-up Signal 1 Check only 早期精选 (Early Pick) Open the 信号类型 (Signal Type) dropdown, uncheck the other five options, and keep only 早期精选 (Early Pick). (The red-dashed box is our annotation on the original screenshot.) 2 Fill in the parameters under 过滤条件设置 (Filter Settings) Early Pick Count (24H) ≥ 3 Time Since Latest Pick (min) ≤ 60 Switch to the 信号 (Signals) tab. Set the minimum for 早期精选次数(24H) (Early Pick Count (24H)) to 3 ; set the maximum for 最新精选距今时长(分) (Time Since Latest Pick (min)) to 60 ; then click 确认 (Confirm) to save. These numbers aren't fixed — if you get too few results, lower the "count" or widen the "time since" window; if your feed is too noisy, tighten them back up. Run with the values above for a day first, then fine-tune to match your own pace. 1 Check only 苏醒信号 (Wake-up Signal) Likewise, in the 信号类型 (Signal Type) dropdown, uncheck the other five options and keep only 苏醒信号 (Wake-up Signal), which specifically catches older tokens that go quiet and then see volume return. 2 Fill in the parameters under 过滤条件设置 (Filter Settings) Wake-up Signal Count (24H) ≥ 1 Time Since Latest Wake-up (min) ≤ 60 Set the minimum for 苏醒信号次数(24H) (Wake-up Signal Count (24H)) to 1 ; set the maximum for 最新苏醒距今时长(分) (Time Since Latest Wake-up (min)) to 60 , to make sure the token has only just woken up.

title: Custom Filtering for the Six Signal Types
heading: Three Example Dashboards
text: Using the same approach, here are three commonly used dashboards. Dashboard Purpose Filter Settings Signal Scanner (信号扫链) Early Pick Quickly scan for early opportunities that just appeared Early Pick Count (24H) ≥ 3 Time Since Latest Pick (min) ≤ 60 Back from the Dead (死而复生) Wake-up Signal Catch older tokens that went quiet and are now seeing volume return Wake-up Signal Count (24H) ≥ 1 Time Since Latest Wake-up (min) ≤ 60 Trending Board (热门榜单) All Six Signal Types Selected Don't filter by signal type — just see the overall hottest tokens right now Signal Type = All Six Signal Types Selected Sort = 24h Heat The sort control for the "Trending Board" is the sort icon in the top-right corner of the list: open it and choose 24小时热度 (24h Heat) under 按代币排序 (Sort by Token), while keeping all six signal types selected. heading: Real Trading Cases
text: Real cases where the strategy fired, reviewed after the fact. More to be added over time. Historical cases — not investment advice. 1 Wake-up Strategy Hit · LAYOOO Flow: Wake-up strategy catches the anomaly → checking X shows the community just kicked off a CTO → don't chase the first wave, wait for a pullback to get filled → combine the signal with the event for a manual entry decision. Strategy logged roughly 10.24x . Take: this case is a clean fit for the Wake-up Strategy's core judgment call — "dead, then revived." First check that it's been dead long enough (a long stretch of low-volume, dormant sideways action), then wait for a CTO move at the moment of revival (community takeover, restarted operations) as the confirming signal. Stacking both conditions is more reliable than jumping in on volume alone. 2 Wake-up Strategy Hit · CZ26 Flow: long stretch of dead, no-volume silence → a Twitter influencer posts a meme about a "Ferrari CZ26 custom supercar" tagging @cz_binance, with the replies full of people betting on whether CZ is making a comeback → the Wake-up strategy catches the anomaly at the same time, flagging two wake-up signals → the rally confirms once the influencer's topic gains traction. Take: same underlying logic as case 1 — dead long enough is the precondition, and an external event/topic picking it back up at the moment of revival (this time not a CTO, but a Twitter influencer meme driving attention and CZ-comeback bets) is the confirming signal. The event type can vary, but the structure — "dormant first, then re-hyped" — stays the same. The strategy fires first, the event confirms it afterward.

title: Strategy Logic and ctx
heading: Strategy Logic: Writing the Decision Code
text: Basic Settings controls "when it triggers and how orders are placed on a hit"; Strategy Logic controls "whether you actually want it once it hits." This is a block of JavaScript — the platform loads data into ctx , and your code decides whether to let a token through or exclude it. Pasting code replaces the whole block — it doesn't append. The editor always holds exactly one script. When you get new code, select all and delete the existing content before pasting — appending it below leaves two blocks of logic stacked on top of each other, which at best duplicates checks and at worst throws errors outright. Remember to click 保存策略 (Save Strategy) in the top right after editing. The Strategy Logic tab. The row at the top shows this strategy's most recently matched tokens; below it is the code editor. Common Patterns in the Code Pattern What It Does return false Excludes this token — it doesn't match. Every "veto" block in the screenshot returns false as soon as it finds a problem. ctx.log.error(...) Writes a log line, viewable in the 实时日志 (Live Logs) tab. It's worth logging the reason and the actual values while excluding a token — otherwise once it's live you won't know why something didn't match. || {} and Array.isArray(...) A safety fallback before reading data. Some data sources aren't available under certain trigger methods (see the table below), and without a fallback this throws an error outright. What's Attached to ctx Data Source What's in It ctx.chip_analysis Chip/holder distribution analysis. The screenshot uses above_percent , below_percent , and top5_holders (an array of the top five holders). ctx.holders The holder list, an array — you can slice(0, 30) to get the Top 30. Each entry has address , total_hold_percent (share of holdings), and transfer_in_percent

title: Settings and Trading Parameters
heading: The Basic Settings Page
text: After importing, all parameters are already carried over — this page is mainly for checking and fine-tuning. The two things you'll typically actually change are the active time window and the buy order amount. 1 Top Half · Trigger Method The four tabs at the top are 基本设置 (Basic Settings), 策略逻辑 (Strategy Logic), 实时日志 (Live Logs), and 清理 (Cleanup); the top right has 保存策略 (Save Strategy) and AI 生成代码 (AI-Generate Code). You must click save after making changes. 2 Bottom Half · Trading and Tiers From the active time window downward: the Auto Trading toggle, order method, amount, wallet, take-profit/stop-loss, and win-rate distribution tiers. Strategy Trigger Method (Choose One of Three) This is the single most important choice on the page — it determines which data this strategy can use. Method How It Triggers / What Data It Can Use Signal-Triggered Driven by signals already on the platform — good for adding one more filter layer on top of a signal. Can use all data: logearn holders kline indicator chip_analysis . All three official strategies use this method. Token Live-Stream-Triggered Covers every token's every-second changes across the whole chain — good for "chain scanning" strategies (new tokens / just graduated / market cap just crossed a threshold). Can only use logearn and signals data — no access to holders or chip analysis. Strategy-Triggered Subscribes to the pool of matched tokens produced by one or more "Token Live Stream" strategies, then re-checks tokens in that pool using richer data. Can use all data — effectively, the live stream does a rough first pass, and this does the fine filtering. Top-Half Parameters Parameter Description Applicable Chain All / Solana / BNB. title: Choosing an Official Strategy
heading: The Three Official Strategies
text: The engine ships with three official strategies preloaded, all live and running with real trading data. You can treat them purely as signals, or turn on automated trading orders directly. 1 1.5-Stage Strategy · Strong-Market Strategy Each strategy is one full block: a bar chart of historical hits on the left, returns and win-rate distribution in the middle, and the six-layer filter counts plus the run/pause toggle on the right. 2 Wake-up Relay Strategy This one has 自动交易 (Auto Trading) checked — once it hits, there's no manual order needed, it's placed automatically. The Wake-up Relay Strategy is best paired with grid orders. Set the buy method to 网格挂单 (Grid Order), the reference price to 当前市值 (Current Market Cap), and the drawdown range to 30% ~ 100% . This way, a hit doesn't trigger a single market buy — instead it lays down limit orders in batches across the drawdown range from market cap, averaging down the cost basis.
